title: Kingdom
description: A sprawling monarchy of crumbling stone and rigid tradition, stretching from fertile inland plains to the storm-battered coast. It is a land of vast, lonely roads connecting isolated settlements, where the crown's influence wanes with every mile traveled from the capital. While trade and agriculture persist, a sense of stagnation hangs over the cantrevs, the old provinces the Kingdom is divided into, allowing stern religious orders and ambitious upstarts to carve out their own domains. The Kingdom functions through inertia, largely ignoring the rot taking hold in its forgotten corners—most notably the notorious Estate on its edge.
summary: A sprawling monarchy of rigid tradition and decaying infrastructure, encompassing the Reformatory, the Harvest House, and the coastal Estate.

title: The Crossroads
description: A meeting of five roads on open ground, a day's ride from the Estate. Hired coachmen will not take the Old Road, so passengers are set down here to wait for the Caretaker. Cold fire-pits, a broken bench and abandoned luggage mark the waiting. The signpost at the centre carries five boards, one for each road, reading Guilt, Loathing, Failure, Regret and Disgrace. Travellers leave coins and small offerings at its base, as people still do at crossroads everywhere.
summary: A meeting of five roads where the Caretaker's coach collects those bound for the Estate; a place between places.

title: St. Martha's Reformatory
description: A grim stone structure perched on a desolate hillside. Its gray walls bear the weathering of harsh seasons, while inside, dormitories lined with iron-framed beds house troubled girls under the stern watch of the Sisters. The branding chamber remains most disturbing, its implements for 'marking the impure' surrounded by stains no amount of scrubbing can remove. Daily routines of prayer, labor, and harsh correction continue in this isolated place where the outside world's judgments cannot reach.
summary: A grim stone structure on a desolate hillside, serving as an isolated institution for troubled girls, known for its strict routines and branding chamber.

title: Woodsman's Cottage
description: A blackened foundation ringed by scorched trees, all that remains of the humble home where the Woodsman and his wife briefly gave shelter to the Runaway. The stone hearth stands amid the devastation, reaching skyward like an accusing finger. Despite years passing, no vegetation reclaims this scarred earth.
summary: A blackened foundation and scorched trees, all that remains of the humble home where the Woodsman and his wife once lived.

title: Harvest House
description: A three-story farmhouse standing proudly among fertile fields, recently expanded as its owners' fortunes have risen. Though still modest compared to true noble estates, the newly-titled Lord and Lady have adorned it with hasty attempts at grandeur. Farm tools and practical implements have been replaced with imitation finery. Local farmers speak of invitations to dine with their former equals, though many note the curious pattern of travelers who never complete their journey to these celebrated feasts.
summary: A three-story farmhouse among fertile fields, expanded by its newly-titled owners, known for grand feasts and disappearing travelers.

title: Servants' Quarter
description: The farmhouse's ground floor, hastily converted from family living space to servants' quarters and food preparation areas. Livestock pens adjoin the kitchen, allowing the Carver immediate access to fresh meat. A sturdy cart with iron wheels stands near the back door, its bed stained dark despite frequent scrubbing. Servants hired from neighboring farms whisper about the master's insistence that all visitors be announced before being allowed upstairs, and the strange sounds that echo through the floorboards during late-night feasts.
summary: The ground floor of Harvest House, converted into servants' quarters and food preparation areas, with adjoining livestock pens and unusual practices.

title: Dining Hall
description: Once the farmhouse's modest common room, now expanded by knocking down walls to create space for a long table surrounded by mismatched chairs acquired from across the region. Candles in tarnished holders provide inadequate light, casting most of the room in shadow while illuminating the heaping platters that never seem to empty. The newly-installed sideboard sags under silver serving dishes that gleam with recent polishing, a stark contrast to the rough-hewn beams overhead where hooks meant for curing meats now hold tapestries awkwardly cut to fit the space.
summary: An expanded dining hall in Harvest House, featuring a long table for feasts, mismatched chairs, and heaping, never-ending platters.

title: Nursery
description: The uppermost floor, once sleeping quarters for a large farming family, now converted into an unsettling nursery despite no announcement of an expected child. The central cradle, built from butcher's blocks joined together, dominates the room with its unusual size and sturdiness. Walls once whitewashed now display crude paintings of feasting scenes, while strings of preserved meats hang from ceiling hooks in place of traditional mobiles. The Lady is often found here, rocking in a chair beside the empty cradle, her swollen form suggesting either impending motherhood or simply the effects of endless consumption.
summary: The uppermost floor of Harvest House, converted into an unsettling nursery with a large cradle made of butcher's blocks and crude feasting paintings.

title: The Bottoms
description: The low country of the Kingdom's southeast coast, old marsh drained and held dry behind earth dykes, sluice gates and pumping mills. Its fields lie flat to the horizon below the level of the sea, with reedbeds and mudflats beyond the dykes, where a broad river splits into mouths on its way to the water. The Bottomers who dig, mend and man the dykes are a conquered people, keeping the sea off land they do not own. Though it has been Kingdom land for many generations, the Bottoms has never been declared a cantrev. Fevers rise from the damp in the warm months.
summary: The Kingdom's drained southeastern lowlands, held dry below sea level by the dykes its conquered people keep.

title: Lowhaven
description: The Kingdom's busiest port, where the river meets the sea. Cranes stand along its quays, and short railways run from the docks to the warehouses and out across the fields, lines the crown has long meant to carry up the coast and inland. The Crownlander quarter and its great church of the Light sit on the one ridge of high ground, an old dune line. Below it, in the low streets that flood first, the Bottomers who work the port leave small offerings to the Loa at the street corners.
summary: The Kingdom's busiest port, its cranes and rail yards worked by Bottomers who live in the streets that flood first.

title: Stillbourne House
description: A great winged house of pale stone in one of the Kingdom's northern cantrevs, perfectly symmetrical, with a columned portico beneath a broad pediment and formal gardens stepping down to a river. Inside, its marble floors are polished bright, and the spotless rooms show little trace of life, save the family's portraits, hung in symmetrical rows along every wall, many of them painted very young.
summary: A pale, symmetrical winged house in the Kingdom's north, its gardens stepping down to a river.

title: The Hedge Maze
description: A hedge maze in the gardens of Stillbourne House, entered beneath an ornate stone arch, with dragons trimmed from the hedge standing guard at its turns. Flowers brought from abroad bloom along its walls. Only its outer paths are still open; the inner hedges have been left to grow together into a solid mass, sealing off its centre.
summary: A hedge maze of topiary dragons and exotic flowers, its centre sealed off by overgrown hedges.

title: The Capital
description: The Kingdom's capital, an old walled city of stone above a river, reached across a long bridge lined with statues of saints and scholars. Inside, crooked cobbled lanes run between tall houses of stone and dark timber, steep-roofed and packed so close they lean toward one another, their narrow pointed windows lit late into the night. Over it all rise the spire of its cathedral and the palace, from which the Regency now governs.
summary: The Kingdom's old, crowded walled capital above a river, seat of the Regency.

title: The University
description: The Kingdom's ancient university, a cluster of old stone colleges around cloistered courtyards, approached up a broad flight of steps. Its learning is handed down rather than questioned. In steep wooden lecture theatres, aged professors read from their lecterns while rows of students copy down what they are told, and anyone who argues back is laughed out of the hall.
summary: The Kingdom's ancient, tradition-bound university, a cluster of stone colleges where professors lecture and students are taught not to question.

title: The University Library
description: A tall Gothic hall standing among the University's colleges, entered beneath a square tower, its long wings lit by rows of pointed windows. Inside, shelves climb to the vaulted ceiling, reached by wheeled ladders. The oldest books are chained to their shelves, and its occult texts are kept in a locked room below, open only to senior scholars.
summary: The University's great Gothic library, its oldest books chained to the shelves and its occult texts locked away below.

title: The Museum
description: A great domed hall of pale stone, holding the collected curiosities of centuries: antiquities, relics and oddities from every corner of the world, many of them bought from explorers who carried them home. Fossil skeletons tower over its central rotunda, and its galleries open onto wings of statuary, old armour and cases of pinned specimens. Lamps often burn late in its offices, where its curators work through the night.
summary: The Kingdom's great museum, a domed hall of antiquities, fossils and curiosities gathered from across the world.

title: The Conveyance Guild Hall
description: The Conveyance Guild's hall in the Capital, a great covered yard of coach sheds, stables and storehouses. Spare wheels are stacked along every wall, smiths fit coaches with iron plating and shutters, and crates of freight wait by the gates for every road in the Kingdom. Above the gate is painted its motto, 'Fair prices, in good times and bad', and the fares chalked on the board beneath it change far more often.
summary: The Conveyance Guild's great coaching yard in the Capital, full of wheels, armoured coaches and waiting freight.

title: The Crossed Swords
description: A tavern beside the Conveyance Guild's yard, under a sign of two crossed swords. Old coach lanterns, harness and wheel-rims hang on its walls, and it keeps the best whiskey on the coach roads. The drivers drink at the front, and the Guild's real business is done at the back, in the curtained booth where the Wagon-Master holds court.
summary: The drivers' tavern by the Capital's coaching yards, where the Conveyance Guild does its real business over whiskey.
